record.content_text:
A **pyramid** is an object that has a polygon as its base and sides that **converge** (meet each other) at one single point. The sides are *not* perpendicular to the base.

There are many real life objects in the form of a pyramid. The pyramids of Egypt are well known.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-024.png]

A pile of eggs can be stacked in a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-025.png]

The roof of a house can be in the shape of a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-026.png]

A pyramid can have any polygon, for example a rectangle, a pentagon, or a hexagon, as its base.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-027.png]

We will focus on a pyramid that has a square as its base.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-028.png]

The properties of a pyramid are:

- A square-based pyramid has five *faces*.

- A square-based pyramid has a square as a *base*.

- The side faces are four equal isosceles triangles.

- The faces of a pyramid meet each other at an *edge*.

- A square-based pyramid has eight edges: four around the base and four formed by the triangular side faces.

- The edges of a pyramid meet each other at a *vertex*.

- A square-based pyramid has five vertices: four at the base and one at the top where the triangles meet each other.

The top vertex has a special name. The edges of the triangles that form the side faces converge at a vertex called the **apex**.

We call a pyramid a "right pyramid" if the line between the apex and the centre of the base is perpendicular to the base.

The side faces are triangles that meet each other at one single point, the apex. **converge** To converge is to move towards each other and to meet at one point. **apex** The apex is the top-most point that is furthest from the base of a 3D object.
record.content_text:
**pyramid** A pyramid is a 3D object that has a polygon as its base. The side faces are triangles that meet each other at one single point, the apex.

**converge** To converge is to move towards each other and to meet at one point.

**apex** The apex is the top-most point that is furthest from the base of a 3D object.

Question 3: What is the shape of the side faces of the pyramid?

Question 4: What is the name of the line labelled $QR$?

Question 5: What is the name of the point labelled $S$?

record.answer_text:
Question 1

Step 1: Recall the properties of a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-034.png]

Step 2: Identify the shaded area and give the correct answer.

The shaded area is a face of the pyramid.

Question 2

Step 1: Identify the shape of the base of the pyramid and give the correct answer.

The base of the pyramid is a square.

Question 3

Step 1: Identify the shape of the side faces and give the correct answer.

The side faces are triangles.

Question 4

Step 1: Recall the properties of a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-034.png]

Step 2: Identify the line labelled $QR$ and give the correct answer.

The line labelled $QR$ is an edge of the pyramid.

Question 5

Step 1: Recall the properties of a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-034.png]

Step 2: Identify the point labelled $S$ and give the correct answer.

The point labelled $S$ is a vertex of the pyramid.

Question 6

Step 1: Recall the properties of a pyramid.

The top vertex has a special name. The edges of the triangles that form the side faces converge at a vertex called the apex.

Step 2: Identify the point labelled $Q$ and give the correct answer.

The point labelled $Q$ is the apex of the pyramid.
